# the contributor audit: quantitative face exhaustion and the linear joint value gap

Source: `candidate 5dc06bb8226350eb`.
Full mathematical read, Sections 1--8: PASS under the stated compact positive
minimal-bad-base framework. No repair required.

The input enlargement has the exact own fiber K_u+tB and all other new fibers
between K_z and K_z+tB. The volume bounds use M=1 correctly; there is no missing
fiber-count factor in C_V. The depth comparison pairs each new mark with an
old point within t, compares measures first and shifts only on the old body.
It is uniform in arbitrary base tilt. The protected minimal faces retain
their entire raw depth functions by exact face isolation.

Thus a base outside the near-deep face union yields an actual competitor with
the same raw maximum and a uniform normalized decrease proportional to eta.
The comparison is with the unrestricted fixed-P ordinary infimum, not with an
artificial compact constraint. Choosing eta=2g/c_F proves the quantitative
cover; the zero-gap case uses exact face exhaustion. Chosen marks have a
uniform positive own inradius from boundary depth zero and the cap slab bound.

The concavity domination constant is valid: a fixed positive anchored weight
at any target base in F_p transfers its value to K_p, and extending the segment
through the source ball transfers it to the actual selected mark. All pairs
are finite, so t_* is uniformly positive. No source is moved off its fiber.

The energy lower bound and own-strip calculation pay every nonvertical cap,
and the separate half-own-volume atomic gap pays the pure-base caps. Large
marked L only helps this lower bound. The two-envelope inequality

    max{g,c_B epsilon-(H-1)g}>=c_B epsilon/H

correctly handles every unknown ratio g/epsilon. Therefore the two-sided
linear JOINT optimized value gap is proved in the explicit framework. This
is stronger than the fixed-body statement and does not assume convergence
rates of minimizing bodies or an optimizer derivative.

The row extension also passes. A true barycentric row is supported on its
source's minimal base face. Affine contact equality identifies L with a
positive touching plane on that row. The same quantitative face estimate
bounds L/L_i by C_0 there, giving original-row <= C_0 tilted-row and
K_V<=log C_0. It gives neither a reverse comparison nor an original-row
barycenter.

The new optimization in epsilon and its extended same-separator equation
remain separate obligations. No sharp Gamma payment follows from this audit.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
